annotations.annotation_text: Page 58 opens Book 1, Chapter 3 ("The Trial of HCE") during the Age of Gods phase. This passage continues the public trial and persecution of HCE, the ballad of Hosty, and the testimony of witnesses, featuring HCE, the Twelve Jurors, Hosty. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 58 ("The Trial of HCE"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Gods dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Tavern/jury motif "Tap" on page 58 ("The Trial of HCE"): the twelve customers drinking in HCE's Chapelizod pub represent public opinion, the Zodiac, and the Apostles within the public trial and persecution of HCE, the ballad of Hosty, and the testimony of witnesses. During this Age of Gods phase, they judge, condemn, and demand another round — the Greek chorus of middle-class Dublin gossip.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
